summary: Analysis of 14 days of CGM and AAPS telemetry (3,995 entries, 98.7% coverage) reveals strong overall Time in Range (86.0%) but elevated hypoglycemia exposure (5.1% TBR), concentrated overnight (23:00-03:00 local time, up to 18.5% TBR) and late afternoon (19:00 local time, 15.3% TBR). Because zero meal carbohydrates are logged, the loop relies entirely on Unannounced Meal (UAM) detection, SMBs, and Dynamic ISF (70%). Highly aggressive dynamic ISF at high glucose levels combined with an excessive 25 U max IOB ceiling causes insulin over-delivery at the tail end of meals, dropping glucose into severe hypoglycemia 2-4 hours later.
strengths: High CGM coverage (98.7% over 14 days) with reliable 5-minute data cadence.
Excellent fasting glucose stability from 06:00 to 09:00 local time (95.2% to 98.7% TIR, average glucose 99-110 mg/dL).
Overall Time in Range is strong at 86.0% with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
DIA setting of 10.0 hours correctly matches exponential insulin decay models to prevent mathematical insulin stacking.
issues: Total Time Below Range (5.1%) exceeds international clinical safety target of <4.0%.
Severe nocturnal hypoglycemia between 23:00 and 03:00 local time, peaking at 18.5% TBR at 01:00.
Late afternoon hypoglycemia spike at 19:00 local time (15.3% TBR) following postprandial glucose excursions.
Complete absence of logged carbohydrate treatments forces total reliance on reactive UAM microboluses.
Max IOB safety limit (25.0 U) is excessively high relative to total daily insulin requirements (~19.7 U/day).

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is excellent at 98.7% with 3,995 entries and minimal gaps. System operational logs and treatment records are complete, though zero meal carbohydrate entries were logged.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid entries, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 min. Total carbs logged: 0.0g across 14 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged carbohydrate entries prevents direct assessment of profile Carb Ratio (CR) accuracy.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic control shows TIR 86.0%, but TBR is elevated at 5.1% (target <4.0%). Hypoglycemia is concentrated overnight (00:00-03:00 local, up to 18.5% TBR) and late afternoon (19:00 local, 15.3% TBR), with extreme lows reaching 41-42 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose summary TBR 5.1%, local hourly TBR at 01:00 (18.5%) and 19:00 (15.3%), glucose extremes list.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No logs for physical activity or hypoglycemia treatment carbs.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight target of 90 mg/dL combined with late evening residual UAM insulin drives nocturnal lows. Fasting basal (06:00-09:00 local) is well-matched, maintaining stable glucose around 100 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target segment 90 mg/dL overnight; local hourly TIR 97.5%-98.7% between 06:00 and 08:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Confounding between late evening meal IOB and basal rate effects on overnight glucose.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U with DIA at 10.0h. CR segments range from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U but are unused due to zero carb logging, leaving UAM and Dynamic ISF to compensate.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile settings (DIA 10h, ISF 56 mg/dL/U), treatment summary showing 0 carb entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: True CR performance cannot be evaluated without logged carb entries.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are continuously active. Unannounced meal rises trigger frequent SMBs up to 20m max UAM basal, accumulating multi-unit IOB during delayed meal absorption.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_always_enabled=true, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20, representative loop statuses showing SMBs up to 1.6 U.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal composition data to assess exact absorption timelines.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF (70%) aggressively shrinks effective ISF to 27-38 mg/dL/U during postprandial spikes >200 mg/dL. Combined with a max IOB limit of 25 U (>125% of TDD), this causes severe over-dosing at meal tails.
Zero prebolusing or meal bolusing occurs. Postprandial glucose peaks at 16:00 local (32.1% TAR) before reactive SMBs force a sharp crash into 19:00 local hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local average BG peaking at 162.8 mg/dL (16:00) and dropping to 105.4 mg/dL (19:00).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb entry records or bolus timing data.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carb entries are not used. Excursions take 4-6 hours to resolve, exacerbated by GLP-1 therapy (1.25 mg weekly) slowing gastric emptying.
analysis_steps.evidence: Therapy response windows showing 240-360 minute glucose recovery times; GLP-1 notes on Aug 14, 17, 20.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing meal composition and carb absorption records.

analysis_steps.findings: The primary driver of hypoglycemia and high variability is reactive over-dosing from UAM SMBs and Dynamic ISF (70%) operating under an excessive max IOB ceiling (25 U) and low overnight target (90 mg/dL). Recommended sequence: 1) Raise overnight target to 100 mg/dL and reduce max IOB to 6 U; 2) Soften Dynamic ISF to 50%; 3) Encourage premeal bolusing.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of telemetry, loop status logs, decision inventory, and treatment records.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Requires user verification of meal entries for 3-5 days to refine profile CR and ISF.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to 100 mg/dL
recommendations.description: Raise the target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00 to reduce persistent nocturnal hypoglycemia (10.1% to 18.5% TBR).

recommendations.title: Lower Max IOB and Max Basal Limits
recommendations.description: Reduce max_iob_units from 25.0 U to 6.0 U (~30% of total daily dose) and max_basal_u_per_hour from 12.0 U/h to 3.5 U/h to prevent dangerous insulin stacking from automated UAM SMB delivery.

recommendations.title: Soften Dynamic ISF Adjustment Factor
recommendations.description: Reduce dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent from 70% to 50% to prevent extreme ISF shrinking during postmeal rises, mitigating late-afternoon reactive hypos.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise profile target to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Telemetry demonstrates recurring nocturnal hypoglycemia (TBR 10.1% to 18.5% between 23:00 and 03:00 local time). Raising the target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL creates an essential safety buffer overnight.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight CGM trends for 3-5 days to confirm reduction in low glucose events before making further profile changes.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max IOB of 25 U (>125% TDD) and max basal of 12 U/h are excessively high. Reducing to 6 U IOB (~30% TDD) and 3.5 U/h max basal provides crucial safety against UAM insulin stacking.
70% Dynamic ISF factor causes severe ISF shrinking (down to 27 mg/dL/U) and reactive hypoglycemia. Softening to 50% stabilizes insulin delivery during high glucose excursions.
Standard absorption parameters for oref1 dynamic model. Keep current values.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Bolus upfront for meals 10-15 minutes prior to eating with 50%-70% of estimated carbs, allowing SMB/UAM to handle residual rises, and use e-carbs over 3-5 hours for complex or GLP-1 slowed meals.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Shift from 100% reactive UAM delivery to proactive meal bolusing prevents initial peak hyperglycemia (32.1% TAR at 16:00 local) and eliminates late-afternoon reactive hypoglycemia drops.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal carbohydrate amounts and bolus timing for 3-5 consecutive days to establish reliable meal profiles.

exceptions.suggestion: Reduce immediate meal bolus to 30%-50% upfront and extend carb duration (e-carbs over 3-5 hours).
exceptions.rationale: Delayed gastric emptying from weekly GLP-1 (1.25 mg) risks early postmeal hypoglycemia if large upfront boluses are given.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Update overnight profile target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00.
Step 2: Lower max_iob_units to 6.0 U and max_basal_u_per_hour to 3.5 U/h in AAPS safety settings.
Step 3: Adjust dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent from 70% to 50% in Dynamic Sensitivity settings.
Step 4: Monitor CGM data for 3-5 days, paying close attention to overnight and late afternoon time below range.
Step 5: Begin logging carbohydrate entries and premeal boluses for main meals to reduce reliance on unannounced meal automation.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithms rely on observed glucose rises before delivering insulin, inherently delaying insulin delivery relative to meal absorption.
Dynamic ISF increases insulin sensitivity factor calculations during high glucose levels; if set too aggressively, it can over-deliver insulin at the tail end of a meal rise.
A safety limit for Max IOB should typically represent 30% to 50% of Total Daily Dose to prevent runaway insulin delivery during sensor artifacts or unannounced meals.
